purpose: Current operational router for archive and collection work. This file supersedes earlier priority snapshots for day-to-day research. It does not alter the frozen surviving-object census.
principle: Prioritize the next source that can close a relation, not the next institution that can add a collection name.

targets.status: S+; first commercial-workshop chain already closed at series level
targets.closed: 1885 Type Slide Nos. 1–2 advertisements, twenty-shilling price and retailer network are matched to surviving Wh.6601 cabinet drawers explicitly labelled TYPE SLIDE No. 1 and No. 2.
targets.next: High-resolution drawers 9–12 and representative Type Slides; transcribe the fifty-species matrices; test whether duplicate drawers are copies, variants, components or storage overflow; search ephemera for orders/price lists/retail correspondence.
targets.payoff: Field collection → preparation method → society notes/slides → standardized commercial Type Slide → retail → surviving workshop reference archive.

targets.target: Quekett Microscopical Club + Oxford RMS collections
targets.closed: Cole publication architecture and institutional Library/Cabinet separation are documented; major society slide collections survive.
targets.next: Search existing QMC label transcription for Cole/Martin/Prize Medal/Studies and diagnostic Volume I subjects; query Oxford old slide indexes against a small set of itemised RMS events.
targets.payoff: Published issue/donation event → historical cabinet record → surviving slide.

targets.target: University of Tokyo Medical Library — Anatomy Department nos. 110, 118–123
targets.closed: Course diary, preparation quantity ledger, manufactured histology/embryology catalogue, microscope/instrument index and practical microscopy records are identified as a coherent 1870s–1880s sequence.
targets.next: Acquire page images with covers and original order; extract columns/numbering first; then test preparation categories across production, instrument and teaching records.
targets.payoff: Potential independent paper on institutional production of practical microscopy in Meiji Japan.

targets.target: Harvard Embryological Collection + Charles Sedgwick Minot papers
targets.closed: Serial sections, original card catalogue, line drawings, previous HEC numbers, modern MCZ numbers, preparation technique fields and publication citations coexist; UK corpus already records Minot's 1877 serial-section microtome and technical programme.
targets.next: Date-filter nineteenth-century HEC records and sample a few series through old number → card/drawing → technique → publication → current number; use Minot correspondence only where the object/publication route generates a question.
targets.payoff: Best control showing seriality without material publication: anatomical sequence versus Cole's subscription sequence.

targets.target: Cambridge Museum of Zoology / Whipple — Balfour serial sections and apparatus
targets.closed: Balfour embryological sections survive; relevant objectives and a 1870s Zoology microtome survive at Whipple; Museum notes original catalogues/notebooks/cabinets in historical collections.
targets.next: Obtain Balfour series inventory and original documentation, then test publication/figure links before assigning any specific apparatus to a specific slide.
targets.payoff: Sectioning apparatus → serial preparation → anatomical sequence → publication.

targets.target: Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn Historical Archives
targets.status: S; item-level catalogue/shipment bridge already exists
targets.closed: Nine of the twelve June 1880 RMS slides strongly match numbered Naples catalogue offerings.
targets.next: Search 1879–1881 preparation-department accounts, copybooks and A. W. Waters correspondence using the matched catalogue numbers and shipment date.
targets.payoff: Catalogue → internal order/dispatch → physical British shipment.

targets.target: Museo de La Plata — Tempère & Peragallo / Möller + Historical Archive
targets.closed: Named historical slide series survive in the same museum that preserves institutional correspondence from 1884 onward.
targets.next: Get current series inventory and label/box photographs first; then search acquisition/exchange correspondence by exact names and series numbers.

targets.target: St Andrews — John Thomas Norman slides
targets.closed: Surviving Norman-labelled slides are explicitly linked by the institution to the 1872 list of 2,584 objects; the UK corpus shows Norman slides in secondary exchange and optical test use, while BNA records a broad Norman slide display in 1862.
targets.next: Transcribe St Andrews Norman labels and current sleeve coordinates; exact-title search against the 1872 list; capture secondary retailer labels separately.
targets.payoff: Public display → catalogue → purchase/resale → test use → institutional survival.

targets.target: University of Coimbra — Costa Simões 1873 catalogue
targets.status: A+; paper system strong, object survival open
targets.closed: One publication joins the histology/physiology course programme, microscopic-preparation collection and experimental-physiology apparatus with 92 engravings.
targets.next: Row-level parse before any archival enquiry; then use category/item names to ask whether original preparations/apparatus survive.
targets.payoff: Published institutional teaching system and a controlled comparison with Tokyo's internal ledgers.

targets.target: Manchester Gibson cabinet / Whipple Pritchard cabinet / Dundee maker series
targets.closed: These surviving cabinets expose maker labels, tray/order information or catalogue-derived labels that can decide which trade catalogues deserve full extraction.
targets.next: Transcribe labels first; then select catalogue rows. Preserve Manchester's published 22-versus-25-tray discrepancy as dated states until the current inventory is checked.
targets.payoff: Buyer cabinet as transaction residue rather than maker catalogue as sole market evidence.

digital_harvest.mode: bounded keyword corpus, not broad archival visit
digital_harvest.stop_rule: Stop after slide/preparation transactions are saturated; do not convert the whole Haeckel correspondence into a microscopy corpus.

hold: Kew aggregate slide collection until a named nineteenth-century transferred subcollection is found.
Zoological Survey of India aggregate slide/type holdings until a pre-1900 accession or named slide series is closed.
Charité/Virchow material until slide-specific preparations or catalogues are identified.
Edinburgh anatomy collections until a microscope-slide/preparation series is explicit.
General national/geographic searching unless it supplies a new mechanism or closes a current actor/series.
